html:
The Assam and Tibet earthquake of 15 August 1950 had a magnitude of 8.7. It is one of the strongest earthquakes ever recorded on land. Its centre lay in the Mishmi Hills, where India's Assam meets southeast Tibet.

It was caused by the collision of the Indian and Asian plates, the same slow crash that raises the Himalayas. About 4,800 people died. Huge landslides blocked rivers in the mountain valleys; when the natural dams burst, floods swept down the Brahmaputra and its tributaries, washing away villages in the plains.

It came at a tense moment. It struck on India's Independence Day, and in October the Chinese army entered eastern Tibet, the start of the Chinese annexation of Tibet. On the chart the same quake also appears in South Asia, as the 1950 Assam earthquake.
